info.title: Reference business API
info.summary: Documented reference integration for the canonical scheduling, billing / claims-status, provider network and referral / authorization contracts (WP-23).
info.description: SYNTHETIC reference service. Writes are change requests keyed by a client-chosen request id: a replay never applies a change twice, a change applied but not finalized is completed by request id, and the lookup by request id is visible within the account's documented visibility window. A write with a dispatch deadline (notAfter) gives up when its final check fails, but absence is proved only by a fence after the deadline (never by a 404 plus elapsed time: a COMMIT can land late). Every answer about a change request carries its request digest. Responses carry Refbiz-Account and Refbiz-Region. Error bodies carry a reason code only.

put.summary: Book an open slot for a client (CLIENT_CONFIRMED by that client).
put.description: Optimistic concurrency on the slot version; 409 SLOT_UNAVAILABLE or VERSION_CONFLICT when it changed.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: Client-chosen request id (the platform derives it from its provider idempotency key). The idempotency identity of the change.

200.description: The change is COMPLETED (first delivery or replay; a replay carries Refbiz-Replayed: true). The body carries the stored requestDigest; a client must not claim the change unless it equals the digest of the request it sent.

409.description: A business refusal (VERSION_CONFLICT, SLOT_UNAVAILABLE, STATE_CONFLICT), DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (the request's notAfter passed before it could be committed) or FENCED (the request id was fenced: nothing can ever be applied under it). Nothing was applied; the request id is recorded REJECTED with that code.

422.description: REQUEST_ID_REUSED: the request id is already used by a DIFFERENT request (operation or body). That earlier request may have been applied: reconcile by GET /api/v1/change-requests/{requestId} and compare its requestDigest; never treat this answer as 'not applied'.

get.summary: Lookup by request id (the reconciliation path). 404 for an unknown id AND for one not yet visible (the index lags by up to the account's visibility window, GET /api/v1/meta/{system}/consistency). A 404 is never proof of absence, whatever time has passed: once the request's notAfter has passed, POST /api/v1/change-requests/{requestId}/fence answers authoritatively. The body carries the stored requestDigest (SHA-256 hex of 'refbiz.request.v1\n' + operation + '\n' + canonical JSON of the request body: sorted keys, no whitespace) so a client can bind the found change to the request it would send. Needs the read scope of the request's system.

post.summary: Completes an INCOMPLETE change request (step 2 only: the receipt); never applies the change again. Replays a COMPLETED one; 404 for an unknown id. Needs the write scope of the request's system.

The proof of absence, allowed once the request's notAfter has passed (database clock). With a change request stored under the id it answers it as stored (no lookup lag; a delivery still inside its transaction is waited for). With nothing stored it records the id FENCED (REJECTED, failureCode FENCED, Refbiz-Fenced: true): no delivery of the id can ever be applied (each is refused 409 FENCED). Before notAfter with nothing stored: 409 FENCE_BEFORE_DEADLINE, nothing changes. Needs the write scope of the operation's system.

200.description: The change request stored under the id, or the fence

409.description: FENCE_BEFORE_DEADLINE: nothing stored and notAfter not passed yet; ask again later.

post.summary: Legacy product: creates an appointment. NOT idempotent: every delivery creates another one. A client creates only under its own reservation of the reference (PUT /api/v1/legacy/references/{externalRef}) and reconciles by GET /api/v1/legacy/appointments/by-reference/{externalRef} and, past its deadline, the reference fence; never by sending again. Refused 409 FENCED under a fenced reference and 409 RESERVED_BY_ANOTHER_DISPATCH under another dispatch's reservation. With notAfter the appointment is created only if the final deadline check passes (409 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED otherwise, nothing stored).

parameters.name: externalRef
parameters.description: Client reference stored with the appointment (not enforced unique)

put.summary: Reserves the reference for one dispatch before its create (the dispatch marker of the non-idempotent product). The first reservation wins; any later one (another dispatch id) answers the stored state with reservedForDispatch false, so a client that creates only when reservedForDispatch is true never sends a second create for the reference. With notAfter no reservation is made after it (409 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED when nothing is stored).

200.description: The reference's state for this dispatch

post.summary: Gives back a reservation whose create was provably never sent (only the reserving dispatch id, only while RESERVED). Otherwise answers the stored state unchanged.

The legacy product's proof of absence, allowed once the create's notAfter has passed (database clock): POSTED when a create committed under the reference (a create still inside its transaction is waited for), otherwise FENCED (a reservation that never created is fenced too): no create can ever be stored under the reference. Before notAfter with nothing stored: 409 FENCE_BEFORE_DEADLINE.

PartialWrite.description: PARTIAL_WRITE: the change was applied, its finalization failed. Complete it by request id; never send a new request.

authority.description: CLIENT_CONFIRMED: the acting party is the record's client. PROVIDER_APPROVED: the acting party is the provider whose schedule it is. A provider approval never stands in for a client's consent.

notAfter.description: Optional dispatch deadline (at most 24 hours ahead). The change is applied only if the final check, the last statement of its transaction (database clock), passes; otherwise the request is REJECTED with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. Lock waits are bounded by the time left. The deadline bounds how long a delivery keeps trying; it does NOT make a lookup 404 definitive (the COMMIT after the final check can land after notAfter). Once notAfter has passed, POST /api/v1/change-requests/{requestId}/fence proves absence. Part of the request digest.
